external_entities.name: member
external_entities.description: A library member who uses the library app to renew loans and reserve books, and uses self-service kiosks.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members borrow, renew and reserve books through the library app on their phones.

external_entities.name: desk staff
external_entities.description: Library desk staff who use the circulation page to extend loans, clear account blocks and mark books returned.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Desk staff can extend a loan, clear a block on a member's account or mark a book as returned by hand
external_entities.notes: Everyone at the desk uses the same shared login; individual staff members cannot be identified.

processes.name: library app
processes.description: A phone application through which members renew loans and reserve books, calling the lending API.
processes.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API.

processes.name: lending API
processes.description: The REST API that checks loan rules, serves the circulation page, and reads and writes the loans database.
processes.source_excerpt: It's a REST API. JSON in, JSON out.
processes.notes: The Lending service note says: "The lending API is internal-only." The Interview transcript says: "The phones talk straight to the lending API over the internet." These are incompatible positive claims about exposure, so exposure remains unknown. Priya said: "I think it checks a token the app gets at sign-in, but I'd have to look." She also said she could not tell what it accepts or does with a call it does not like; this is a hedged gap, not an authentication value. The API is one service with no queue in front of it.

processes.name: self-service kiosk
processes.description: A branch kiosk where members scan their library card and books they are borrowing or returning, then sends the loan or return to the lending API.
processes.source_excerpt: The kiosks are in every branch and they send each loan and each return to the lending API as it is scanned.
processes.notes: Priya could not say what the kiosks talk to beyond what arrives at the lending API.

data_stores.name: loans database
data_stores.description: The single database containing members, loans and reservations, including names, email addresses, home addresses and full borrowing histories.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Names, email addresses, home addresses and every member's full borrowing history live in the loans database.
data_stores.notes: Priya corrected the earlier statement about two databases: "We merged those in the spring. It's one loans database now. The old reservations database is gone."

data_flows.name: renew or reserve
data_flows.description: A member uses the library app to renew a loan or reserve a title.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members borrow, renew and reserve books through the library app on their phones.
data_flows.data_description: Loan renewal or reservation request involving the member and a book or title.

data_flows.name: submit loan change
data_flows.description: The library app sends a member's loan renewal or reservation request to the lending API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API. It says which book and which member
data_flows.notes: Priya said: "I think it checks a token the app gets at sign-in, but I'd have to look." Authentication is therefore unknown.
data_flows.data_description: The specified book or title and member information for a loan renewal or reservation.

data_flows.name: send loans returns
data_flows.description: A self-service kiosk sends a scanned loan or return to the lending API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The kiosks are in every branch and they send each loan and each return to the lending API as it is scanned.
data_flows.data_description: A loan or return, including the scanned member card and book.

data_flows.name: update loans
data_flows.description: Desk staff use the circulation page served by the lending API to extend a loan, clear a block or mark a book returned.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Desk staff can extend a loan, clear a block on a member's account or mark a book as returned by hand, through a circulation page the lending API serves.
data_flows.notes: Everyone at the desk uses the same shared login, and the history records only that the loan was closed by hand.
data_flows.data_description: Loan updates and member-account changes, including manual returns and account blocks.

data_flows.name: read and write
data_flows.description: The lending API reads from and writes to the loans database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The API is the only thing that reads or writes it.
data_flows.data_description: Member records, loans, reservations and borrowing history.

trust_boundaries.name: branch network
trust_boundaries.description: The network used by branch kiosks and desk staff.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The kiosks sit on the branch network.

trust_boundaries.name: council data centre
trust_boundaries.description: The council data centre where the lending API and loans database run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The lending API and the loans database run in the council data centre.

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The external network over which phones reach the lending API.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The phones talk straight to the lending API over the internet.
trust_boundaries.notes: This describes how the API is reached, not where the API runs; the API remains placed in the council data centre.

assumptions.assumption: The loans database contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the database contains names, email addresses, home addresses and every member's full borrowing history; these are personal and commercially sensitive records.
